- If sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; reduce forecast by 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- Model shows persistent lag in mean reversion; if price is below 10-day moving average for 3+ days, forecast should be slightly above average to avoid under-correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; reduce first 5–7 days by 0.5–1.5% to align with observed volatility.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast if price has moved >1.5% in last 5 days.
